title: Trace span consolidation and latency-heatmap playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic approach for reducing trace noise from tokenized inference microcalls by consolidating spans into meaningful anchors and exposing a compact latency heatmap dashboard. Goal: make operator investigations fast (minutes) without losing the ability to drill into raw spans for genuine anomalies.

Context & motivation:
- Tokenized LLM inference produces hundreds of tiny spans per request: per-token decode, KV cache lookups, kernel exec fragments, post-processing hooks. Full retention of all spans creates high storage/query cost and noisy dashboards.
- Existing sampling strategies either drop too much context (hard to correlate stage regressions) or retain everything (expensive). We need a mid-path: deterministic consolidation for common fast flows + full-trace retention for anomalies.

High-level design:
1) Span consolidation rules (server-side before export)
   - Request anchors: retain an explicit top-level span labeled request.anchor with request_id, model, route, tenant, start/end timestamps, and coarse stage latencies (decode, kv_lookup, kernel_exec, postproc).
   - Stage aggregation: group contiguous micro-spans into named stage spans: e.g., decode.batch, kv.lookup, kernel.exec. Each stage span keeps aggregated stats (count, min, p50, p90, p99 of micro-span durations) and a fingerprint list (up to 5 micro-span ids) for later sampling.
   - Merge heuristics: if micro-spans are < 2ms and repeated > 5x in a request, compress into an aggregated repeated-run counter rather than separate spans.
   - Exception passthrough: spans that carry error flags, non-OK statuses, or unusually high single-span duration (> 2x p99 baseline) are marked for full retention and not consolidated.

2) Sampling & retention policy
   - Headline traces: store consolidated anchors for 100% of requests for real-time dashboards and heatmaps. Anchors are lightweight (O(1) spans per request).
   - Full-trace retention: keep 1% of requests as full traces by deterministic sampling keyed on hashed request_id + tenant, plus 100% retention for traces flagged by exceptions or anomaly detectors.
   - Burst capture: if a route triggers an SLO breach (p99 > threshold) for a 5-minute window, escalate sampling to 10% and retain full traces for the next 30 minutes for forensic analysis.
   - Cost-aware TTL: consolidated anchors retained for 90 days; full traces kept for 14 days by default, configurable per-tenant.

3) Instrumentation changes (minimal invasive list)
   - Add request.anchor span at the caller boundary (inference gateway or runtime entry).
   - Emit stage markers when entering/exiting: stage.name and stage.{start,end}_ts so server-side collector can aggregate without changing all downstream span-producing libraries.
   - Error tagging: standardize error tag keys (error.code, error.phase, error.msg) so consolidation can identify passthroughs.

Dashboard/Heatmap layout (operator-first)
- Panel A: Request volume by tenant + route (time series) with a small table showing consolidated p50/p90/p99 per-route (from anchors).
- Panel B: Latency heatmap (rows = routes, columns = time buckets) colored by p99 anchor latency — quick visual for sustained regressions. Filter by tenant and model.
- Panel C: Stage-slice waterfall (per-route): stacked bars showing median stage durations (kv, decode, kernel, postproc) so stage-level regressions surface immediately.
- Panel D: Anomaly cohort list: top anomalous traces (by deviance from baseline) with quick links to full-trace links (if available).
- Panel E: Sampling health and retention cost estimate (daily GB, estimated query cost).

Metric mapping and naming conventions
- anchor.request.duration_ms (histogram or summary) — primary SLI source (use anchors not micro-spans).
- anchor.stage.{kv,decode,kernel,postproc}.duration_ms — stage-level quantiles.
- trace.sample.rate — per-route sampling rate exported by collector.
- trace.full_retained — boolean counter when a trace is flagged for full retention.
- span.compress.count — count of micro-spans compressed into an aggregated stage span (useful for debugging consolidation fidelity).
- error.phase.count — aggregated errors bucketed by phase to help triage.

Alert proposals (operational, low-noise)
- Alert 1 (route SLO): route anchor p99 > configured SLO for 3/5 consecutive 1-minute windows -> page on-call; auto-escalate sampling to 10% for the route.
- Alert 2 (stage regression): anchor.stage.kernel.p95 increases by >3x baseline and stage share >40% of request latency -> notify infra + serving-runtime on-call (likely kernel/kernel-scheduling).
- Alert 3 (sampling health): trace.sample.rate deviates from expected by >50% -> alert observability infra (sampling config drift).
- Alert 4 (spike without full-traces): consolidated p99 surge but full-trace retention rate < 0.5% -> create a PSAT ticket to capture more traces automatically.

Operator quick actions (within dashboard)
- Toggle route-level sampling to 5/10/100% (writes to sampling config service).
- Trigger on-demand full-capture for a tenant/route for N minutes.
- Link to pre-filled incident template with affected routes, time window, top anchors.

Investigation workflow (playbook)
1) Spot: heatmap shows route with sustained p99 elevation.
2) Verify: check Panel A for volume spikes and Panel E for sampling health.
3) Escalate sampling: flip sampling to 10% for 30 minutes from dashboard (auto-trigger available).
4) Correlate: open anomalous full-traces from Panel D; inspect stage breakdown on anchor and expand fingerprinted micro-span ids to fetch raw micro-spans if needed.
5) Hypothesize & fix: use stage-slice waterfall to identify whether regression is decode vs kernel vs kv and follow area-specific runbooks.
6) Postmortem: capture consolidated metrics and representative full-trace ids for long-term storage.

Edge cases & cautions
- Multi-model fanout: when a request fans out to multiple models, create sub-anchors per-model and a parent request.anchor. Heatmap should be able to roll up both ways.
- Cold-cache detection: use session-warmth heuristic (session_warmth_index from prefix cache hits) to tag anchors; panel filters should allow isolating cold-cache vs warm-cache latency.
- Privacy/PII: ensure consolidated anchors redact prompt text and only include hashed content identifiers. Full-trace retention should respect tenant-configured PII policies.

Implementation roadmap (quarterly milestones)
- Q1: collector-side stage marker parsing + anchor span injection; basic consolidated anchor export.
- Q2: dashboard heatmap + sampling toggles + deterministic sampling by tenant.
- Q3: auto-escalation on SLO breaches + cost meter and TTL controls.
- Q4: rollout per-tenant retention configs + runbook automation.

Open questions / discussion items:
- What is the ideal micro-span duration cutoff for consolidation? (2ms is a starting heuristics; need cluster-wide sampling to iterate).
- How do we surface consolidated vs raw-latency differences to customers using Dedicated/Private? (expose both metrics but document differences).
- Operator UX: should escalation actions be gated by RBAC and audit logs? (yes, need approver workflow).

Next steps (owner: Jin Park)
- Sync with serving-runtime team on stage markers (task: OBS-3421).
- Prototype anchor exports in sandbox and evaluate dashboard widgets on synthetic tokenized traffic (owner: Evelyn Zhao).
- Draft alert thresholds with SRE and product (owner: Marco Ruiz).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: anchors first, full traces second. Aim is operator velocity and predictable cost.
- Please comment inline on sampling %s and retention TTLs (we will iterate with telemetry cost numbers).

References:
- Trace strategy doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Strategy
- Sampling RFC: OBS-3421
- Collector PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/754
